hero.title: About the Circle
hero.left: A private circle for chief executives, built on trust rather than reach.
hero.right: The Circle was formed on a simple observation: the people who most need candid counsel are the least likely to be offered it.

photo.alt: Above, circle and business people in meeting for teamwork, collaboration or talking in office and workplace. Group, conversation and together for professional planning, negotiation or b2b mockup
photo.note: Interior of a considered, quiet room — the setting the Circle meets in.

story.title: Our Story
story.lead: The Circle began as a standing invitation between a handful of chief executives who had run out of rooms in which they could speak plainly.
story.body: What began as an occasional dinner became a structure — pillars, councils, a framework of trust — because the value turned out to sit in the regularity rather than the occasion. The form has changed a good deal since. The premise has not.

sections.title: Our Purpose
sections.lead: To hold a room in which leadership can be discussed honestly.
sections.body: The Circle exists to make candour ordinary between people who rarely encounter it. Everything else — the forums, the councils, the briefings — is built to serve that, and is dropped when it stops serving it.

sections.title: Our Beliefs
sections.lead: Four convictions shape how the Circle works.
sections.body: That counsel is worth more than advice. That a small room outperforms a large one. That confidence, once given, is absolute. And that a network is measured by the quality of a single introduction rather than the length of a list.

sections.title: Our Mission
sections.lead: To be the room a chief executive keeps returning to.
sections.body: Not the largest gathering in the calendar, nor the most visible — the one that proves useful enough to survive a tightening diary. The Circle would rather be indispensable to a few than familiar to many.

sections.title: Our Vision
sections.lead: A standard for how senior leaders convene.
sections.body: That private, considered, confidential conversation becomes the expectation at this level rather than the exception, and that the Circle is held as the reference for how such rooms are run.

sections.title: Who We Serve
sections.lead: Chief executives and chairs of established organisations.
sections.body: Members carry final responsibility for an organisation of substance — the accountability that cannot be delegated to anyone else in the building. Sector, geography and scale vary widely across the membership. The seniority and the disposition do not.

philosophy.title: Leadership Philosophy
philosophy.quoteNote: Pull-quote placeholder — this slot must carry real words from a real, named person. Nothing should be written on their behalf.
philosophy.support: Leadership at this level turns less on having answers than on the quality of the questions a person is willing to sit with. The Circle is built around that conviction, and everything in it follows from there.

differences.title: What Makes Us Different
differences.intro: Four things the Circle does differently, and holds to when it would be easier not to.

features.label: Closed by design
features.body: The Circle does not grow towards a target. Membership is bounded by what a room can hold, and admission is slowed rather than accelerated.

features.label: Counsel, not content
features.body: There is no keynote and no stage. Members come to be questioned by peers rather than addressed by speakers.

features.label: Confidence as the first term
features.body: Discretion is not a policy applied to the Circle. It is the condition that makes the Circle possible at all.

features.label: Built to compound
features.body: Councils and forums hold their membership across the year, so context accumulates instead of resetting at every meeting.
